prose.label: Private Access.
prose.text: {{zpa-rule}} {{zpa-stray}} What the stray-traffic rule is meant to catch is not stated {{gap:zpa-predefined-purpose}}.

Same-named ZIA Forwarding Control rules are a different product's policy: [[zia.forwarding-control.predefined-rules]]. Whether the Terraform provider stops a predefined rule from being deleted is covered in [[cloud-connector.terraform.rule-protection]].

checks.do: Whether a predefined Direct rule is enabled at all (they ship disabled) and whether the device is in gateway mode.
For dropped Private Access traffic, whether it matched the view-only ZPA Pool For Stray Traffic rule.

default-zia.statement: A default forwarding rule with a default gateway is predefined for Internet & SaaS: each tenant comes with a default rule that forwards internet-bound traffic to Internet & SaaS using automatically selected gateways.

quotes: A default forwarding rule with a default gateway is predefined for Internet & SaaS.
By default, each Cloud Connector tenant comes with a default rule to forward internet-bound traffic to Internet & SaaS using automatically selected gateways.

zpa-rule.statement: A ZPA Forwarding Rule with a default gateway is created when the tenant subscribes to the Private Access license.

quotes: ZPA Forwarding Rule with a default gateway is created when you are subscribed to the Private Access license.

zpa-stray.statement: ZPA Pool For Stray Traffic is a rule with the Drop method, created automatically with view-only access when a ZPA server's SKU is enabled on the Cloud or Branch Connector.

quotes: ZPA Pool For Stray Traffic with the forwarding method set to Drop is automatically created with view-only access when you enable a ZPA server's SKU on your Cloud or Branch Connector.

direct-rules.statement: Three predefined Direct rules, disabled by default and shown according to the tenant's licenses, send to Direct traffic whose destination is the Zscaler Cloud Endpoints application service group, a WAN IP group, or a LAN IP group.

quotes: They are disabled by default, but you can enable them. Predefined rules appear based on the licenses enabled in your tenant:
Direct rule for Zscaler Cloud Endpoints: This rule states that if the destination is a Zscaler Cloud Endpoints application service group, then the forwarding method is set to Direct.
Direct rule for WAN Destinations Group: This rule states that if the destination is a WAN IP group, then the forwarding method is set to Direct.
Direct rule for LAN Destinations Group: This rule states that if the destination is a LAN IP group, then the forwarding method is set to Direct.

gateway-mode-only.statement: These predefined rules apply only to hardware devices deployed in gateway mode; they can be enabled only once a location or Branch Connector group is configured for them, and only gateway-mode devices can join that mandatory group.

quotes: Predefined forwarding rules are only applicable to hardware devices deployed in gateway mode. Additionally, you can only enable predefined forwarding rules if you have configured a location or Branch Connector group for them.
Zscaler only allows devices deployed in gateway mode to be a part of the mandatory group used for these rules.

editable-fields.statement: On predefined forwarding rules only Rule Order, Rule Status, Location/Sublocation and Cloud & Branch Connector Groups can be edited.

quotes: You can only edit the Rule Order, Rule Status, Location/Sublocation, and Cloud & Branch Connector Groups fields for predefined forwarding rules.

zpa-predefined-purpose.title: What ZPA Pool For Stray Traffic catches
zpa-predefined-purpose.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the rule "is read-only and catches stray ZPA-server traffic". The help gives only its method (Drop), view-only status and creation trigger.
zpa-predefined-purpose.blocks: explaining Private Access traffic dropped by this rule
